overview: Two hormones from the pancreas with opposite jobs, keeping blood glucose levels balanced.
genZNote: Insulin: 'okay blood sugar, calm down.' Glucagon: 'okay blood sugar, wake up.'

aspects.label: Secreted When
aspects.valueA: Released when blood glucose is high (e.g. after a meal).
aspects.valueB: Released when blood glucose is low (e.g. during fasting).

aspects.label: Source Cells
aspects.valueA: Beta cells of the pancreatic islets of Langerhans.
aspects.valueB: Alpha cells of the pancreatic islets of Langerhans.

aspects.label: Main Mechanism
aspects.valueA: Promotes glucose uptake by cells and glycogenesis in the liver.
aspects.valueB: Promotes glycogenolysis and gluconeogenesis in the liver.

overlay.examHighYieldNote: Type 1 diabetes results from insufficient insulin production, while glucagon excess/imbalance is less commonly the primary clinical focus.
overlay.memoryTrick: Insulin brings sugar IN (lowers it). Glucagon lets glucose GO (raises it).
overlay.commonMisconception: Insulin and glucagon are not produced by the same pancreatic cells — beta cells make insulin, alpha cells make glucagon, both within the islets of Langerhans.
